Class Abilities

1st Level

Hunter's Edge

  • Effect: Your weapon hits deal +1 damage, improving to +2 at 6th level, +3 at 9th, +4 at 12th, +5 at 15th, +6 at 18th, +7 at 21st and +8 at 24th. Against your marked prey or favoured enemy it is +1 at 1st to 3rd level, then +1 more at every even level from 4th, to +12 at 24th.

Marked Prey

  • Effect: Once per encounter, as part of an attack, mark a creature you can see.
  • The mark lasts the encounter, on one creature at a time.
  • While it is your marked prey, you have Advantage on your first attack roll each round against it and on Track checks to follow it.

Woodcraft

  • Effect: You are Trained in Survival, Tracking, Set Snares and Climb (Book II) in the wilderness, on top of your starting skills, and Master in Tracking from 5th level. You read tracks (a trail's condition from 3rd level, the creature type from 5th), find food and shelter for yourself without a check and for 2d4 others on a Moderate check, and set and disarm wilderness traps (the Ranger Progression Table gives your trap search bonus and trap damage).
  • Conceal and Move Silently (Dexterity): in the wilderness, no penalty at half speed or slower, Disadvantage above it, impossible while running.
  • While Concealed you count as Hidden.
  • From 5th level you may attempt both together, at quarter speed, with Disadvantage on both.
  • Delay/Neutralise Poison (Wisdom): For natural poisons familiar to the ranger (those of their home region and their favoured enemy). On a successful check: delay the poison's effects for 1 hour per level (no action, 1 attempt only).
    • If the roll exceeds the needed total by 6 or more: neutralise the poison entirely (effects already suffered are not reversed)

2nd Level

Light Step

  • Effect: You may Move Silently or Conceal at up to full speed in natural terrain without Disadvantage.

Hunter's Tricks

  • Effect: On one hit of your choice against your marked prey each round, choose one: Hamstring (its speed is halved until the end of its next turn), Pin (until the end of its next turn, it can't move away from you without a Reflex save against your Class Save DC) or Expose (the next ally to attack it has Advantage). From 8th level, your Quarry Strike's hit can carry a trick too.

3rd Level

Favoured Enemy

  • Effect: Choose one specific creature type as favoured enemy (GM should require a creature encountered repeatedly in the character's history).
  • Against your favoured enemy, one hit of your choice each round deals an extra weapon damage die and ignores its resistance; it has Disadvantage on Hide checks against you, and its first attack against you each round has Disadvantage.
  • You have Advantage on checks to track it and to neutralise its poisons.
  • 13th level: choose a second favoured enemy

4th Level

Hunter's Quarry

  • Effect: Marked Prey may be used twice per encounter, on different creatures.

5th Level

Quarry Strike

  • Effect: When you use your action to attack, make one additional weapon attack as part of it, with Disadvantage (see Extra attacks in The Arneyan Codex).
  • No Disadvantage against your marked prey.
  • If it drops your marked prey, you may mark a new creature you can see at once, without spending a use of Marked Prey.

6th Level

Apex Predator

  • Effect: Once per day, when you use Marked Prey, for the encounter your marked prey has Disadvantage on Hide checks against you, can't Disengage from you, and you know where it is while it's within 60ft; a creature that turns invisible stays marked.
  • 24th level: you may use Apex Predator twice per day, and you have Advantage on checks to track, corner or finish your marked prey

7th Level

Find Passage

  • Effect: Examine terrain you have some experience of and find the least obstructed path: halves any movement penalties for terrestrial terrain. Anyone travelling with the ranger has their penalties reduced by one-quarter.

9th Level

Survival Instincts (Wisdom)

  • Effect: Advantage on checks to avoid being surprised; from 17th level you are never surprised in the wilderness.

10th Level

Advanced Tracking (Wisdom)

  • Effect: After a successful track check, determine accurately the number in the tracked party, their make-up (war band, hunting party, etc.), whether well or lightly armed, their speed, and their habits.
  • A second successful Wisdom check (+1 only) can predict their intended direction of travel; a third can identify their specific destination

13th Level

Relentless Hunter

  • Effect: Every hit against your marked prey deals the Favoured Enemy extra weapon damage die and ignores its resistance. When it drops, you may mark another creature you can see as part of your next attack, without spending a use of Marked Prey.

15th Level

  • Dexterity Bonus: permanent +1 Dexterity. It can take the score past 20, to 22 at most (see The Mortal Limit in Character Creation).

20th Level

Renown: Lodge of the March

  • Effect: You may found a lodge of the March (see Renown in The Arneyan Codex); each season 1d6 scouts and one 1st-level Ranger join it. While you hold it, you can't be surprised within a day's travel of it.

Paths and Kits: Ranger Traditions

Each kit is an item in the Kits compendium, in the Ranger folder. Drag one onto your character.

Choose one Path (Hunter, Beast Master or Wild Warden) and one Kit at character creation.

  • Your Path is how you hunt, with features at 1st, 5th and 10th level; your kit is where you learned, with one improvement at 9th.
  • The peoples, orders and places a kit names are examples, not the only ones: a kit suits anyone from a tradition like it.
